headline.requestedStatement: paper/Generating_Antichains_Simplified.tex:240–244, lem:splitting: “For all $m,n\in\mathbb N$, \[ \alpha(m+n)\le\alpha(m)+\alpha(n+1). \]” The paper explicitly states at line 192: “Throughout the paper, $\mathbb N=\{1,2,\ldots\}$.”
headline.leanStatement: AntichainOfGivenSize/Model/Theorem.lean:129: theorem alpha_splitting (hprior : Prior) (m n : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) : alpha (m + n) ≤ alpha m + alpha (n + 1)
headline.why: Read independently, Lean asserts the displayed inequality for every pair of positive natural numbers, given the fieldless proposition Prior. This matches the paper exactly: hm and hn encode its explicit positive-natural convention (paper-states-it), rather than adding restrictions. Prior is an empty structure, inhabited by ⟨⟩; its binder is a harmless modelling artifact, with no borrowed mathematical result. Both universally quantified parameters, all three occurrences of alpha, the addition operations, the constant 1, and the inequality direction correspond. The definition of alpha minimizes the cardinality of a finite generating family over arbitrary finite ambient universes; BasicLemmas.lean proves existence and attainment, so sInf is not concealing an empty minimization domain. Finite relabelling preserves the paper's objects. The proof follows the paper's disjoint-ground-set construction. The underlying splittingLemma additionally permits n = 0. Verification evidence supports the proof: the supplied elaborator output lists only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; saved lake build --wfail and model-check commands have recorded exit code 0 and successful output. All 138 recorded source hashes match the inspected files, with no unrecorded project Lean files. Source scanning found no proof holes or custom trust mechanisms; the three partial definitions belong to audit tooling. No build was executed during this review. To reproduce the headline axiom and closure checks, run `lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true AntichainOfGivenSize/Model/Theorem.lean` from the project root. Probability-denotation review is not applicable to this deterministic lemma.

auditSurface.why: The finite-set representation matches the indexed-family definition after deduplication and padding. Lean also permits B = 0; its K > 0 guard preserves nonempty indexing.

auditSurface.claims: For some c > 0, the fraction of integers 5 ≤ n ≤ N satisfying c times the logarithmic scale ≤ alpha n tends to one.

auditSurface.claims: For every sufficiently large real X, the maximum alpha n over positive integers n < X lies between positive constant multiples of the logarithmic scale at X.
auditSurface.why: Ico 1 ⌈X⌉₊ implements exactly the strict cutoff n < X. The two positive constants expand the Theta assertion.

auditSurface.claims: Shared positive c and C provide an eventual upper bound, density-one lower bound, and simultaneous density-one bounds for natural and real cutoffs; separate positive constants give the eventual extremal order.
auditSurface.paperSays: paper/Generating_Antichains_Simplified.tex:156–170 states both main bounds and concludes “$\alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{n})$” for almost all positive integers and “$\max_{1\le n<X}\alpha(n)=\Theta(\growth{X})$”.
auditSurface.why: All main-theorem components are present. The natural- and real-cutoff density formulations make equivalent consequences explicit; the paper does not require the extremal constants to equal c and C.

## Correspondence with the paper

The lemma at `paper/Generating_Antichains_Simplified.tex:240–245` asserts

\[
\alpha(m+n)\le\alpha(m)+\alpha(n+1).
\]

At `AntichainOfGivenSize/Model/Theorem.lean:129`, `AntichainOfGivenSize.alpha_splitting` states the same inequality for natural numbers `m` and `n`, with hypotheses `hm : 0 < m` and `hn : 0 < n`. These hypotheses exactly encode the paper’s explicit convention at line 192 that natural numbers are positive. The arguments of `alpha`, additions, constant `1`, and inequality direction all agree.

The additional parameter `hprior : Prior` carries no mathematical premise: `Prior` has no fields, is inhabited by `⟨⟩`, and is unused by the splitting proof. Likewise, `[DecidableEq V]` in `generatedIdeal` supplies finite-set infrastructure without imposing an additional mathematical hypothesis on callers.

The definition correspondence supports this statement-level match. `AntichainOfGivenSize.generatedIdeal` represents the union of the generators’ powersets. `AntichainOfGivenSize.alpha` minimizes generator cardinality over unrestricted finite ambient universes, and `BasicLemmas.lean` establishes both existence of witnesses and attainment of the minimum. Thus the infimum does not conceal an empty feasible set. Finite relabelling preserves the paper’s objects, with no ambient-size restriction or antichain prerequisite introduced.

There are two extensions beyond the paper’s positive-input formulation: `alpha` also has a value at zero, and `AntichainOfGivenSize.splittingLemma` at `BasicLemmas.lean:169` permits `n = 0`. Neither changes the requested inequality on the paper’s domain. The proof follows the paper’s construction: it takes optimal families, embeds them into disjoint ground sets, establishes that their generated ideals intersect exactly in the empty subset, and bounds the combined generator count.
